findings.element: .card[aria-expanded] / .card[data-open] — src/tasks.js:52 declares `let openNoteId = null; /* the card showing its full note */`, read at src/tasks.js:428 (draggable), :430 (aria-expanded), :434 (data-open) and :2828 (Escape → "Note closed."); consumed by src/tasks.css:954, :956, :957, :1179, :1976
findings.problem: openNoteId is never assigned anything but null. Every one of the fourteen assignments in tasks.js (542, 554, 661, 2829, 2899, 3098, 3319, 3476, 3632, 4185, 4367) sets it to null; nothing sets it to a task id. Measured consequences: every card with a note ships a permanent `aria-expanded="false"`, `draggable` is permanently "true", `data-open` is never emitted, so five CSS rules can never match — including tasks.css:954 `.card[data-open] .cardNote { max-height: none }`, the rule that was supposed to release the five-line note clamp, and tasks.css:1179's open ring. The Escape branch at 2828-2832 (`say("Note closed.")`) is unreachable, so that sentence is in the build and can never be spoken. Driving it confirms the mechanism moved: a real mouse-down/up on `.cardTitle` opens `.taskPanel`, moves focus into it and announces "Task open." — the in-place disclosure the comment on line 52 describes does not exist. Separately, CDP Accessibility.getPartialAXTree on the card returns role=article with focusable/describedby/keyshortcuts/roledescription and NO `expanded` property at all: `aria-expanded` is not supported on role=article, so even a correct value would never reach a screen reader.
findings.fix: Delete the dead state rather than resurrect it. In src/tasks.js: remove `openNoteId` (line 52) and every assignment; make line 428 `draggable="true"` unconditional; delete the `aria-expanded` term on line 430 entirely (role=article does not support it — the panel is a separate object and announces itself through the live region already); delete the `data-open` term on line 434 and the Escape branch at 2828-2832. In src/tasks.css delete lines 954, 956-957, 1179 and 1976. If the five-line note clamp still needs a way out, hang it off the panel that actually opens (`.taskPanel`), not off a card attribute nothing sets.

findings.element: .b-layout [data-layout-to] / [data-app="timeline"][data-layout] — src/timeline.js:176-178 `PHONE_T.addEventListener("change", function () { if (C.rootEl()... ) go("owner-flight"); })`, in the core IIFE that opens at src/timeline.js:26; `C` is only declared at src/timeline.js:331, inside the renderer's separate closure
findings.problem: `C` is not in scope at line 177, so every crossing of 720px throws `ReferenceError: C is not defined` (measured: Chromium pageerror at MediaQueryList.<anonymous>, on 768→721→700 and again on 700→900) and the re-mount never runs. The file's own header comment at src/timeline.js:4-8 states the contract this handler exists to keep — "the across composition is withheld on it, and crossing it re-mounts the owner's surface so the bar is never stale" — and it is not kept. Driven: load timeline.owner-flight at 1024 (data-layout="across", the Across/Down group present), resize to 700 → data-layout stays "across" and the Across/Down buttons are still on screen at phone width, against the locked decision "Across is never offered on a phone". `acrossAllowed()` (src/timeline.js:620) reads `!PHONE_T.matches` correctly, but only at render time, and nothing re-renders. The reverse is as bad: load at 700 (down, no toggle), widen to 1024 → still down, toggle still absent, so a desk user who narrowed the window once can never get the across composition back. The gates cannot see any of this because both open a fresh page per viewport and never cross the boundary.
findings.fix: Replace the body of the handler at src/timeline.js:177 with a plain re-mount in the scope it actually lives in — `mount();` — and nothing else. Do NOT call `go()`: `go()` (src/timeline.js:2318-2326) moves focus to `.b-pressTitle`/`.b-who`, and stealing focus to a heading because somebody dragged a window edge is a worse defect than the one being fixed. Add the same one-line remount to the tasks/notes pattern already in use (`PHONE.addEventListener("change", () => mount())`, src/tasks.js:4203) so all three products cross 720 the same way, and add one assertion to interaction-check.mjs that resizes an open page across 720 in both directions and requires zero pageerrors plus `[data-layout-to]` absent below 721.

findings.element: [data-app="tasks"][data-density="compact"] .when — src/tasks.css:2167 `[data-app="tasks"][data-density="compact"] .when { height: 18px; font-size: 10.5px; ... }`; the state is switched at src/tasks.js:3204-3208 from the Show menu's Display row (src/tasks.js:800)
findings.problem: Compact is a real, one-click state — Show → Compact, `root.setAttribute("data-density", "compact")` — and sixteen CSS rules key off it, but it is not in elevate.config.json's `states` list, so neither gate ever visits it. Driven (open Show, click Compact, at 1440 and at 1280): `.when` computes to font-size 10.5px, which is off the declared typeRamp in elevate.config.json (steps 10 and 11 exist; 10.5 does not). The same 10.5px is inherited by the `.sr` span inside it. In comfortable the same element is 11px, on the ladder. So the surface has a reachable configuration that would turn the `ramp` category of the currently-green measured gate red, and a half-pixel type size that buys 0.5px per glyph on the one piece of card metadata an operator reads on every row. The `sizeLadder`/`spaceLadder` exemption recorded in notes.ladders does not cover this: `typeRamp` IS declared in this config and IS gated.
findings.fix: Two edits. (1) src/tasks.css:2167 — set `font-size: 10px` (the ramp step below) or keep 11px and take the row height out of the type instead; nothing else in the suite is set at a half pixel. (2) elevate.config.json — add `tasks.compact` to `states` (the state handler already accepts it, and add the density to the state setter if it does not) so the density the operator can actually pick is inside the five-viewport audit rather than beside it. Then re-run gate.mjs and fix whatever else compact turns up.

findings.element: [data-app="notes"] .darkActs / .darkAct — src/notes.css:1889 `.darkActs { display: flex; ... flex: 0 0 auto; margin-left: auto; }`, src/notes.css:1007 `.darkAct { ... height: 44px; padding: 0 20px; }`, and src/notes.css:1787 `.darkAct kbd { display: none; }` which lives inside `@media (pointer: coarse)` opened at src/notes.css:1770
findings.problem: In notes.voice the dictation overlay's action pair cannot shrink or wrap, so it forces the whole DOCUMENT to scroll sideways. Measured: `.darkActs` renders 440px wide at left:32, needing 472px of viewport; `.darkAct` ("Stop and read it back" + a 63px `<kbd>Ctrl Enter</kbd>`) is 296px with no min-width:0. Driven at height 844: without mobile emulation documentElement overflow is 152px @320, 82px @390, 42px @430, 12px @460, 0 from ~472; WITH the gate's own isMobile/hasTouch emulation it is still 28px @320. The only rule that relieves it hides the keycap under `@media (pointer: coarse)`, so a narrowed desktop window — which is exactly how WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow is tested, and what a 1280px desktop at 400% zoom becomes — never gets it, and neither does a 320px phone. 1.4.10 (AA) requires no two-dimensional scrolling at 320 CSS px; this state fails it in both pointer modes. The gate cannot see it because config.viewports starts at 390 and marks it isMobile, and `@media (max-width: 900px)` at src/notes.css:1893 only lets `.darkFoot` wrap — it never touches `.darkActs`. This is the same class the 2 September ledger already closed once for notes.review ("the one state in the suite that scrolled sideways at 390 was the one the gate never walked"); it is back, one state over.
findings.fix: Append these three rules to the END of src/notes.css (after line 1900) — NOT into the `@media (max-width: 720px)` block, which spans :1581-1755 and therefore sits BEFORE the `.darkActs` base rule at :1889, so an override written there loses the cascade at equal specificity and is dead: `@media (max-width: 720px) { [data-app="notes"] .darkActs { flex: 1 1 100%; flex-wrap: wrap; margin-left: 0; min-width: 0; } }`, `@media (max-width: 720px) { [data-app="notes"] .darkAct { flex: 1 1 100%; min-width: 0; justify-content: center; padding: 0 12px; } }`, `@media (max-width: 720px) { [data-app="notes"] .darkAct kbd { display: none; } }` — and delete the now-duplicated `[data-app="notes"] .darkAct kbd { display: none; }` from the `@media (pointer: coarse)` block at :1787, because the keycap is unreadable at that width whatever the pointer. Verified by inserting exactly these rules at the tail of the live sheet: documentElement overflow goes to 0px at 320/390/430/460 in BOTH pointer modes, both pills stay 44px tall (256px wide at 320, 326px at 390), and 768 and 1440 are byte-identical. Then add `{ "name": "320x844", "width": 320, "height": 844 }` WITHOUT isMobile to elevate.config.json's viewports so the WCAG reflow width is gated in both pointer modes instead of only the touch one.

findings.element:
[data-app="notes"] h1.headName / li.idxSection > h3.idxDay — src/notes.js:1628 `

All your notes

`, killed by src/notes.css:1595 `[data-app="notes"] .headName { display: none; }` inside `@media (max-width: 720px)`; the day groups at src/notes.js:2128 `

`
findings.problem: Notes is the only product of the three whose heading outline is wrong, and it is wrong two different ways. At a desk the accessibility tree reads heading[1] "All your notes" followed straight by five heading[3] day groups — level 2 does not exist anywhere in the product, so the outline skips a level on the surface a person spends most of their time on. At ≤720 `display: none` removes the h1 from the tree entirely (display:none prunes, it does not merely hide), so on a phone notes.notebook offers five level-3 headings under nothing, and notes.review offers a lone level-2 "Worth doing something about?" under nothing. Measured with page.accessibility.snapshot at 390 and 1440 across all four Notes states. Tasks keeps h1 "The Orchard, events" (plus five h2 lane names at a desk) at both widths and Timeline keeps h1 "Mara & Finn" plus two h2s at both widths, so this is Notes' defect alone, not a suite decision. The gate cannot see it: interaction-check.mjs never inspects heading levels, and the audit does not model the accessibility tree.
findings.fix: Two edits. (1) src/notes.css:1595 — replace `[data-app="notes"] .headName { display: none; }` with the visually-hidden treatment already defined at src/shell.css:89: `[data-app="notes"] .headName { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; margin: -1px; padding: 0; overflow: hidden; clip-path: inset(50%); white-space: nowrap; border: 0; line-height: 1; }`. The h1 leaves the phone head's flex flow exactly as `display: none` did — driven at 390, the head measures 118px high before and after and documentElement overflow stays 0 — but the outline regains its root. (2) src/notes.js:2128 — emit `<h2 class="idxDay">` and drop the now-redundant `role="heading" aria-level="3"`. Verified: the tree becomes h1 "All your notes" + five h2 day groups at both 390 and 1440, with no visual change (`.idxDay` is styled by class, not by tag).

biggestWin: The keyboard and place-keeping floor is the best thing here, and it is not a claim — it measures. All 32 cards on the dense board are reachable from one tab stop by arrows (BFS over all four keys from the rover, zero unreachable), and across a 40-press down-walk and a 12-press cross-lane walk the focused element never once left the viewport. Crossing 720px in Notes with a sentence half-typed carries the draft, the caret offset and focus from .topField to .phoneField and back, with exactly one field in the document at every width. The seam announces every step it takes — "5 words picked", the privacy contract on peel, "Sent to Tasks. Your note stayed here." — lands focus on "Open in Tasks" and leaves a real undo behind it. Focus rings are routed through one outline-only rule per product and composed controls carry the ring on the wrapper (.dockField:focus-within) rather than doubling it. Zero duplicate ids, zero unresolvable aria-labelledby, zero unnamed interactive elements once labelledby is resolved, zero dead class names in 500KB of CSS, and zero clipped strings across nine states by fifteen widths. That is the plumbing the defect library says costs the most, and it is clean.
